sources.entry: rustypaste - Minimal file upload/pastebin service. MIT Rust

summary.one_liner: Rustypaste is a minimal, self-hosted file upload and pastebin service written in Rust that stores files on the filesystem with no database.
summary.what_it_does: Users upload files or text with curl (multipart form or stdin via a helper function) and receive a URL to fetch them back. It supports random or pet-style filenames, optional expiration times with flexible units, one-shot files and URLs that can only be viewed once, and password-protected files using Argon2id hashing. It can also shorten URLs and pull a file from a remote URL. Server features include optional basic auth tokens, a DELETE endpoint gated by delete tokens, an optional JSON file list endpoint, MIME type handling, and a customizable landing page. Configuration is done through a config.toml file with hot reloading support.
use_cases: share files with my team via a private server
temporary file hosting with auto-expiring links
one-time link sharing that deletes after first view
command-line upload of files and stdin with curl
notable: No database: files are stored directly on the filesystem
One-shot files and URLs that can only be viewed once
Password-protected files with auto-generated passwords and Argon2id hashing
Packaged for Arch Linux, Alpine, FreeBSD, and crates.io
caveats: Authentication is optional; without AUTH_TOKEN or token settings the server requires no auth
The DELETE endpoint is disabled unless delete_tokens are configured
Large uploads through a reverse proxy like nginx may need client_max_body_size raised
